Kuvitus: pakkasaamu pihalla. Vasemmalla: Illustration: a frosty morning in a yard. On the left a garage whose door is open and in which a warm light is on; a compressed-air hose hangs on the wall. In the yard stands a car that has been outside all night: there is frost on its roof and windows. The red column of the thermometer on the outer wall of the garage is low. In the background snowy spruces and a pale morning sky.
Pylväskuvio mittakaavassa: renkaan ilman: Bar chart to scale: the total pressure of the air in a tyre at two temperatures. Each horizontal bar is divided into two parts: the air pressure 101 kPa and the gauge pressure shown by the gauge. In the warm garage, +20 °C, the gauge pressure is 230 kPa and the total pressure 331 kPa. After a night of frost, −20 °C, the total pressure is 286 kPa and the gauge pressure 185 kPa. The total pressure has decreased in the ratio of the kelvin temperatures, but the gauge reading has decreased by 45 kPa, that is, by about a fifth.
Lämpövoimakoneen energiavirrat yhden kie: Energy flows of a heat engine during one cycle, arrow widths to scale. At the top the hot source, whose temperature is T1. From it a wide heat arrow Q1 = 1000 J comes down into the engine. From the engine a narrow green arrow, the work W = 350 J, goes to the right, and a heat arrow Q2 = 650 J goes down to the colder environment, whose temperature is T2. The outgoing arrows together are as wide as the incoming arrow.
Kuvaaja: ruiskun ilman tilavuus V lämpöt: Graph: the volume V of the air in the syringe as a function of the temperature θ, with θ from 0 to 80 °C. The vertical axis starts at 36 millilitres. Eight black points at the temperatures 5, 15, …, 75 °C, each with a vertical uncertainty bar of ±0.3 ml. A rising straight line is fitted to the points, passing between them. Two points of the line far apart are circled, (0 °C; 37.7 ml) and (80 °C; 48.5 ml), from which the slope is read: about 0.135 ml per degree.
Kuvaaja: sama suora koko alueella θ = −3: Graph: the same line over the whole range θ = −300…100 °C and V = 0…50 ml. The measured points are only in the range 5–75 °C. The fitted line is extended as a dashed line, and it crosses the temperature axis at about −279 °C. Two grey extreme lines, the steepest and the least steep line that still pass through all the uncertainty bars, cross the axis at about −265 °C and −294 °C. The accepted value −273 °C lies between them.
Voimakuvio: vaakasuora lasilevy kapeana: Force diagram: the horizontal glass pane as a narrow rectangle, while the lift accelerates upwards and the partial vacuum is the smallest possible. The pad is shown in grey in the middle of the upper surface of the pane. The weight G starts from the centre of the pane straight down. The force of the pressure difference F p starts from the upper surface of the pane at the pad and points up, and it is longer than the weight, because the pane accelerates upwards. In this limiting case the normal force from the rim of the pad is zero. Separately, an orange acceleration arrow a upwards.
Voimakuvio: pystyasentoon käännetty lasi: Force diagram: the glass pane turned upright as a narrow vertical rectangle, the pad on the left surface of the pane, in grey. The weight G from the centre straight down. The force of the pressure difference F p pushes the pane from the right horizontally to the left, towards the pad. The normal force N from the rim of the pad pushes the pane from the left horizontally to the right; it is as large as F p. The static friction F μ0 starts from the upper left corner of the pane and points up, and it is longer than the weight, because the pane accelerates upwards. N is about 1.7 times as long as the friction, because at the smallest partial vacuum the friction is 0.60 times the normal force. Separately, an orange acceleration arrow a upwards.
Käsitekartta. Ylhäällä solmu paine: p =: Concept map. At the top the node pressure: p = F / A. Three branches go down from it. Liquid: pressure at depth p = p0 + ρ g h, gauge pressure ρ g h and total pressure, which is the air pressure and the gauge pressure together. Gas: the ideal gas law p V = n R T, the combined gas law p V / T = constant and the kelvin temperature T = θ + 273.15 K. Heat engine: work done by a gas W = p ΔV, conservation of energy W = Q1 − Q2 and efficiency eta = W / Q1.
